daily_summary.html:
Domestic Politics

DPR Speaker Puan Maharani outlined 12 oversight agenda items during the opening plenary session of the DPR's second sitting period, which was attended by 403 members. The oversight priorities range from the wiretapping scandal involving President Prabowo to social assistance programmes. Puan praised the police for uncovering the illegal wiretapping of the president, and in reference to the case involving former National Police Chief Listyo Sigit, she stressed that security forces must not become tools of power.

  • The controversy over Vice President Gibran's academic credentials continued to dominate parliamentary discussions, with PKB considering exercising its right to make a formal statement on the matter, while PDI-P called such a right the most rational approach to the controversy.
  • Puan told legislators not to speculate about Gibran's status and warned against creating public unrest, emphasizing that Gibran remains vice president.
  • Puan said she has not yet received the presidential letter regarding the replacement of the TNI commander.
  • Puan is gathering input from parliamentary factions before the DPR takes further steps on the proposal to impeach Vice President Gibran.
  • The DPR described the working group on past human rights cases as a new chapter for justice in Indonesia.
  • The DPR received a presidential letter to discuss a draft law on asset forfeiture.
  • Police convened an ethics trial for Inspector General Ahrie Sonta, a suspect in the wiretapping of President Prabowo.
  • National Police Chief rotated 25 high-ranking officers and mid-level officers in a reshuffle.

Foreign Policy & Defence

Former Vice President Jusuf Kalla urged Turkey to consider the Aceh peace model as a framework for resolving the Kurdish conflict. Kalla, who played a key role in mediating the Aceh peace agreement, suggested that Indonesia's experience could offer lessons for Turkey's long-standing struggle with Kurdish separatism. His remarks come as Indonesia continues to position itself as a mediator in regional and international conflicts.

  • Indonesia and Australia are piloting joint fire management efforts in East Kalimantan, with the two countries targeting 100,000 liters daily capacity to fight forest fires.
  • Immigration authorities detained three Pakistanis over suspected visa abuse.

Other

The government announced eligibility requirements for the 2026 wage subsidy assistance programme, a key social protection measure aimed at supporting low-income workers. Bank Indonesia reported that retail sales trends are expected to increase through March 2027 due to major religious holidays. Indonesia's exports rose 5.58 percent through September, according to a minister's statement.

  • BYD has significantly narrowed the gap with market leaders in Indonesia's automotive sector, with the top 10 best-selling car brands showing Toyota and Daihatsu under pressure from the Chinese electric vehicle manufacturer.
  • Lazismu, the Muhammadiyah zakat agency, recorded Rp827.69 billion in zakat collection at the opening of the 2026 Muhammadiyah Zakat Summit.
  • Indonesia is seeking innovative funding mechanisms for national park conservation efforts.
  • BNPB identified three companies suspected of burning land in Papua.
  • The government proposed stronger copyright protection for content creators in a move to update intellectual property laws.
